slide_title: Fruit Type & Seed Dispersal: Seed Germination
original_text: Fruit Type & Seed Dispersal Seed Germination When seed germination occurs, the embryo resumes growth and metabolic activity Length of time seeds retain their viability is quite variable Some seeds do not germinateuntil they have been through a dormantperiod Temperate zones -Cold Weather For some, cannot germinate until fruit removed due to inhibitors Environmental requirements for seed germination Availability of oxygen for metabolic needs Adequate temperature for enzyme activity Adequate moisture for hydration of cells
explanation: Seed germination is the resumption of embryonic growth and metabolic activity. Seed viability is variable. Many seeds require a dormant period to prevent premature germination: in temperate zones, seeds may require cold exposure, while others cannot germinate until chemical inhibitors in the surrounding fruit are removed. Germination requires three environmental conditions: 1) Oxygen (for cellular respiration), 2) Adequate temperature (for enzyme activity), and 3) Adequate moisture (for cell hydration).

questions.q: What are the three essential environmental conditions required for seed germination?
opts: Carbon dioxide, light, and soil nutrients
Oxygen, adequate temperature, and adequate moisture
questions.exp: Germination requires oxygen for respiration, an adequate temperature for enzymes, and moisture to hydrate the cells.

questions.q: Why do some seeds fail to germinate until their fruit is removed?
opts: The fruit blocks oxygen from reaching the seed coat.
The fruit tissue contains chemical growth inhibitors.
The seeds require mechanical abrasion by wind.
The fruit is too heavy for the radicle to emerge.
questions.exp: For some seeds, chemical growth inhibitors present in the fruit prevent germination until the fruit tissue is removed.
